row.Finding: Nanovia PP CF, despite the added cabron fibres, still has a tendency to unstick from the printing surface. By adding a soluble HIPS raft and supports the polypropylene is held in place.
row.Exposure / conditions: Own pictured Nanovia HIPS raft/PP-CF support demonstration; links identify G081-10 and G083-04. No adhesion force, geometry, printer conditions, interface strength or load qualification. One shared fact recorded on HIPS; affected PP-CF question also linked in campaign packet.

row.Finding: High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS), as its name indicates, has a very high shock resistance. This resistance also makes it suited as a base 3D printing material, especially for press tools.
row.Exposure / conditions: General HIPS declarative maker context within own article; no exact-product press-tool load, impact/lifetime test or qualified use. Not a material suitability pass.

evidence.text: High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS), as its name indicates, has a very high shock resistance. This resistance also makes it suited as a base 3D printing material, especially for press tools.
